subject: Performance anomaly: customer-facing p99 spike + proposed mitigation & customer note
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: alerts@pager.inc
Date: 2027-04-11T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: [Incident] P99 spike on hosted-us-west model-pool-3 - initial triage

Team,

Monitoring opened an incident at 08:03 PT for a sustained p99 latency spike on the hosted-us-west pool serving model variants for PulseAI (heavy long-sequence traffic). Summary so far: 
- Window: 07:58 - ongoing
- Impact: p99 doubled from ~820ms to ~1.9s; tail and some 95-99.9s more impacted.
- Affected route(s): /v1/generate (model: rdx-g-3b-family and fallback variants) for a subset of PulseAI traffic (identified by client_id).
- Immediate action: shifted approx 40% of incoming requests for PulseAI to a quantized fallback bucket (rdx-g-3b-q4) to reduce memory pressure; enabled KV cache priming for hot prefixes for that bucket.
- Current status: tail improving but still elevated; throughput reduced ~12% for that client during mitigation window.

Attachments: metrics-snapshot-20270411.png (early spike graphs), mitigation-runbook-v1.pdf (runbook notes).

Open questions I need from product/eng before we send customer-facing comms: 
1) Can we authorize a short-lived soft-rate-limit for individual API keys (30-60s) as a stop-gap? Product: is this acceptable operationally (impact on SLAs)?
2) Is a rollback to previous kernel selection feasible (Dylan / infra) for this pool? What risk/time?
3) For the customer note: do we keep the messaging technical (describe fallback + kernel issues) or high-level (we experienced transient tail impact; mitigation in place)? Sales/CS: what tone do we want for PulseAI?

I will coordinate with SRE on timeline if we opt for kernel rollback + canary. Please advise ASAP — PulseAI is on a high-traffic campaign and they will expect a proactive update.

Connor
SRE - Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Thanks Connor — good triage. Quick answers / asks from product: 
- Soft-rate-limit: acceptable as a short-term protective measure but needs explicit approval from commercial (Marissa) for any customer-facing throttling; also update SLA/usage records for potential credit calculation.

Operational asks for engineering:

- Hannah, can you simulate the current request distributions against rdx-g-3b-q4 in the performance lab while we roll canary so we understand error/latency tradeoffs?

I'll draft a short customer note once I have confirmations on the above. If legal/commercial wants to pre-approve wording, ping me.

Karthik

--- DRAFT CUSTOMER NOTE ---
From: Marissa Cole (Redwood Inference)
To: Ellen Rodriguez, PulseAI Ops
Subject: Brief service impact & mitigation actions — April 11

Hi Ellen,

We observed a transient increase in request latency on April 11 affecting a subset of requests from PulseAI. Our team identified the cause in our serving layer and immediately executed mitigations (redirecting a portion of traffic to a quantized fallback, priming caches, and adjusting kernel selection).

What we did:
- Reduced memory pressure via quantized fallbacks and cache priming
- Implemented focused routing to isolate impact to the smallest scope possible
- Monitoring in place and a canary rollback plan prepared if needed

Impact: some requests experienced higher tail latency for a ~20–45 minute window; core throughput and correctness were preserved.

Next steps: we continue to monitor and will follow up with a technical appendix if you want more detail. If this incident materially impacted your SLAs, we will coordinate credits/error reconciliation as appropriate.

Apologies for the disruption — we know PulseAI is running a high-priority campaign and we appreciate your patience.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Growth, Redwood Inference

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T09:19:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [Incident] P99 spike on hosted-us-west model-pool-3 - kernel rollback feasibility

I can prepare a kernel rollback and a 2-node canary in us-west-2 within ~25 minutes. Risk: a rollback will reset some kernel-level optimizations (expected CPU spike + short GC) and could make tail worse for very long sequences for a few minutes during cutover. My recommendation: run the canary, measure 15 minutes, then either promote or revert.

If we promote: expect a short window (~3–5m) of increased error rate during the promotion; we'll keep traffic steering to quantized fallback until the canary is green.

Dylan
Infra/Serving Runtime

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [Incident] P99 spike on hosted-us-west model-pool-3 - mitigation update

Update: at 09:42 we kicked off Dylan's canary (2-node rollback kernel). At 09:56 the canary metrics showed p99 back to ~780–900ms for the canary traffic slice and error rates within baseline. We promoted the kernel to the remaining nodes with traffic steering still favoring q4 fallback for heavy sequences. At 10:02 we enabled a 30s soft-rate-limit for the most aggressive PulseAI API key (internal ops only) as a temporary protective measure (commercial approved).

Current status at 10:05: p99 trending down to ~920ms cluster-wide; monitoring panels attached. We will keep a watch window for 2 hours and prepare a post-incident timeline + RCA.

Connor
SRE - Redwood Inference
